title: Southport killer accused of throwing boiling water mixed with sugar at prison officer
description: Axel Rudakubana is accused of grievous bodily harm and two other assaults of prison officers while serving a life sentence.
body: Axel Rudakubana appeared at the court hearing wearing a pale grey and blue tracksuit top Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has appeared in court accused of throwing boiling water mixed with sugar at a prison officer. The 20-year-old is charged with the attempted grievous bodily harm of a prison officer at HMP Belmarsh, having allegedly thrown the boiling mix through the hatch in his cell door on 8 May last year. He is also charged with two other assaults of prison officers, as well as possession of a knife or other offensive weapon while in prison. Rudakubana, who is serving a life sentence for murdering three children at a dance class in Southport in July 2024, appeared via video link at Westminster Magistrates' Court wearing a pale grey and blue tracksuit top. He spoke only to confirm that he could hear the chief magistrate, and to give his name and date of birth. He rested his head on his left hand throughout the hearing. Prosecutor Catherine Pattinson told the court that prompt medical attention prevented the prison officer Rudakubana is alleged to have attacked on 8 May from suffering any lasting injury. The prosecution also accused him of threatening to soak a female officer outside his cell if she did not pass him a newspaper on 6 May 2025, then throwing an "unknown liquid" at her through his door hatch. Then, on 28 October last year, he allegedly punched a male prison officer in the face. The prosecution said the officer was trying to establish whether Rudakubana had taken his medication at the time. The offensive weapon charge relates to sharpened stone shards that the prosecution say had seemingly been prised from the floor of the defendant's cell. They were found stuck to the under side of a shelving unit in his cell. Pattinson told the court that "when questioned by a prison officer, he said that he was keeping them for self-defence". Rudakubana, who appeared from Broadmoor secure psychiatric hospital, was not asked to enter pleas during the hearing on Monday. He was remanded into custody to appear at the Old Bailey on 19 October. He is currently serving out a life sentence over his deadly attack on a Taylor Swift dance class in July 2024, in which he murdered nine-year-old Alice da Silva Aguiar, six-year-old Bebe King, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven. Rudakubana was also convicted of the attempted murder of eight other children and two adults during the attack. title: Helen Jenner announced by Nigel Farage as new leader of Reform in Wales
description: Farage said it had been untenable for former leader Dan Thomas to continue after his arrest last week.
body: Farage described Jenner as a "determined campaigner" on the steps of Wales' parliament Nigel Farage has announced Helen Jenner as the new leader of Reform in Wales, replacing Dan Thomas after his arrest on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour. Speaking on the steps of the Senedd in Cardiff on Monday, Farage said: "I've known Helen for many, many years. She is a determined campaigner." Farage said he was sorry for former leader Thomas's "personal difficulties", but said it had been untenable for him to continue. "We could have done without this bump in the road," he said. Jenner, who served as Thomas's deputy alongside her role as Senedd member for Bangor Conwy Môn, said it was an honour to be elected to the top job. A leadership vote was held by Reform's 33 Senedd members on Monday morning, in which BBC Wales understands Jenner's colleague Jason O'Connell stood against her. O'Connell had not been expected to stand. Speaking to reporters outside the Senedd, Farage said there would be a vote for a new Welsh deputy leader to replace Jenner on Tuesday. Dan Thomas had steered Reform to its best-ever result in a Senedd election in May, becoming the second-largest party in Wales Jenner had been interim leader and favourite to replace Thomas, with sources telling BBC Wales that "very senior" Reform figures had backed her. Thomas stepped down on 15 September after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour. He was bailed pending further enquiries, and denies doing anything wrong. He was not on the steps of the Senedd for Jenner's unveiling as leader, but he remains a Reform MS after chief whip Llŷr Powell said he had not considered removing the whip from him. After he stepped down, Thomas had been among the Reform Senedd members who met in Cardiff Bay last week to discuss their next steps, with a party official from London attending to oversee proceedings. title: BBC removes 11 Mitchell and Webb comedy sketches from iPlayer
description: The corporation said it had included "the ones that still work today and not the ones that don't."
body: The BBC has removed nearly a dozen comedy sketches from That Mitchell and Webb Look after deciding they no longer "work today". The Bafta-winning comedy, starring David Mitchell and Robert Webb, originally ran for four seasons between 2006 and 2010. The show recently returned to the BBC's iPlayer to mark its 20th anniversary. But 11 old sketches, including one that reportedly showed the comedy duo satirising racism while in blackface, have now been cut. A BBC spokesman said in a statement: "This is a 20-year-old sketch show; in consultation with the programme makers, we have included the ones that still work today and not the ones that don't." The Times reported, external the removed material included scenes featuring war re-enactors in blackface, a sketch about a contestant on a makeover show wearing a burka and a "tribe" living in a garden centre. BBC news has asked Mitchell and Webb - who rose to prominence on the Channel 4 sitcom Peep Show - for a comment. That Mitchell and Webb Look grew out of a similar radio show titled That Mitchell and Webb Sound, which began on Radio 4 in 2003, and went on to win the Bafta for best comedy programme in 2007. Defending the double act, fellow comedian Dom Joly, of Trigger Happy TV, questioned the BBC's "censorship" of itself. Joly told The Times: "I totally get it if the BBC is putting out something really racist, which is laughing at and encouraging other people to feel that it's OK to do that. "But it's so clear that Mitchell and Webb are not doing that. Their intent was not to be racist." Jimmy Mulville, the co-founder of Hat Trick Productions which makes Have I Got News For You, told the same newspaper he could understand the corporation's predicament. "The BBC are in an impossible position," he said. He added that producers had "to be careful", though, "that this is not the thin end of a wedge where we cut things out". Mitchell and Webb are not the first comedians to have had their work edited or removed in recent years, as societal attitudes have shifted. Some artists themselves also began reassessing their work in the aftermath of the Black Lives Matter movement. Matt Lucas and David Walliams' hit show Little Britain was removed from iPlayer, Netflix and BritBox in 2020, after objections resurfaced about some of their characters portraying people from different ethnic backgrounds. At the time, both the BBC and Britbox noted how "times have changed" since the Little Britain first aired in the early noughties. The show is now back on iPlayer but, like Mitchell and Webb, some sketches have been removed. title: Countryside buses resurging in England after years of decline - check your local figures
description: A rise in bus miles with council funding might be starting to reverse the reduction in services.
body: Wiltshire Connect is a demand responsive service - one of the ways some councils are tackling a lack of transport in rural areas Council-funded rural buses described as a "lifeline" by some are enjoying a resurgence after years of decline and new laws are giving authorities more power. Does this mean buses are back in business? Government data shows council support for local buses is rising. With the exception of London, 17% of bus miles travelled across England were supported financially by government. That's down from almost a quarter in 2010, with bigger drops in rural areas, but it is up from a pre-pandemic low of 13% in 2019-20. However, fewer of us have been catching the bus. Journeys per person in England stood at 88 in 2010 and that number was down to 63 by 2024-25. Numbers dropped sharply during the pandemic and a recent rise has not returned them to pre-Covid levels. Figures for 2024-25 show the councils providing the most support to their bus networks tended to be in rural areas. The charity Bus Users UK described supported bus services as "fundamental to social inclusion" and "a lifeline, not a choice" for many. "Without them, people can become isolated and less able to participate fully in their communities," a spokesperson said. Wiltshire is one of those rural areas. The council is one of those across the country attempting to tackle this using DRT - demand responsive transport. West raises thousands for Nepalese flood victims Charity shop helps to 'bankroll' village carnival Solar farm to be built near M4 despite concerns It is a type of on-demand service that passengers book in advance when it is needed and the bus route changes depending on where people need to go. In 2021, the Department for Transport provided £20m to 15 local authorities in England to trial DRT via the Rural Mobility Fund. The Wiltshire Connect service has been rolled out in different areas across the county. It has 13 minibuses operating across three zones and first launched in 2023. There have been 250,000 journeys since, a spokesperson for Wiltshire Connect said. Martin Smith, from Wiltshire Council, said he sees DRT as the future Councillor Martin Smith, the cabinet member for transport in Wiltshire, explained it has been more "affordable" for the council. "If we weren't doing this we'd be trying to subsidise a lot of rural bus routes taking very, very few people from place to place and here we have a solution where it's a couple of buses which move around the area all the time," he said. People book via an app or over the phone and the cost is the same as an ordinary bus service. Passengers have the option to be picked up from various spots close to them and travel to areas within a certain zone. The council still subsidises other services, which are contributing to their supported mileage rather than the DRT. It was expected at first that older people would mostly use DRT but the council said it had found younger people "piling in there". Smith said: "If we can get the younger generation used to using public transport then they will continue to do that potentially through their adult lives." Wiltshire Connect driver James said passengers "love it" One passenger, Cat Jones, and her family started using the service when they moved from London to Wiltshire. They had not needed a car at their previous home and they said the buses were a "lifesaver". She said: "In Wiltshire, you sometimes need more flexible transport than the scheduled buses allow and that's what Wiltshire Connect is. "Everybody is smiling. You feel plugged into the community." James, who is a Wiltshire Connect driver, said: "They [the passengers] love it. "It's a service that has helped so many people be able to get out. "I think some of them feel quite trapped, especially in the smaller villages." This video can not be played How can rural bus services be improved? Bus Users UK has described the overall mileage increase as "encouraging". A spokesperson said: "It shows targeted investment can work but mileage alone does not tell the full story. "A bus service is only useful if it enables people to make the journeys that matter - whether that is getting to work, attending a hospital appointment, accessing education or staying connected with friends and family." It emphasised that the decline before the pandemic was down to local council budget cuts forcing them to "abandon" routes. It said that to get people confident in using the bus again, long-term funding for networks "that people could rely" on was needed. The Campaign for Better Transport said that the publication of a national bus strategy in 2021 had made "the value of buses more explicitly understood and authorities have had the option to step in and plug gaps in provision thanks to dedicated government funding". Silviya Barrett, of Campaign for Better Transport, said: "It is great news that these services are now increasing but overall bus provision is still at a lower level than in 2010 and our mapping shows that many areas still do not have the bus service they need." The Local Government Association has a similar view. It described the recent investment in services as "good" but said it also wanted to see "sustained levels of funding" to encourage people to use buses. The government announced more funding last year as well as the Bus Services Act which gives local authorities more power over the buses in their area. It is not just rural council-backed services that have shrunk. The miles on the buses - for commercial routes too - have been slowly dropping since 2010. There has been a drop of about 22% since 2010. It is back on the rise but has yet to reach the same levels as pre-Covid. Commercial bus miles decreased by a quarter between 2010 and 2025. title: Why Cardiff is set to win race to host Fury-Joshua
description: Why Cardiff is set to beat competition from London and New York to host the long-awaited fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.
body: Anthony Joshua's fight against Tyson Fury is set to be held in Cardiff The long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua is expected to take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday, 11 December. While BBC Sport understands final details are still being hammered out between Netflix, Saudi Arabian organisers Sela and both fighters' camps, Cardiff has firmly emerged as the frontrunner, with an official announcement expected this week. It marks another dramatic twist in a saga that, only weeks ago, appeared destined for New York. A date at Madison Square Garden was so close to completion that plans were already being drawn up for a Manhattan news conference. Instead, after Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to stage the fight on British soil, the Welsh capital has taken centre stage. BBC Sport takes a look at how Cardiff became the leading candidate to host what would arguably be the biggest event in British boxing in the 21st Century. Wembley Stadium was long assumed to be the natural home for a meeting between the two defining British heavyweights of their generation. However, the path to making the fight was complicated by Joshua and Fury having signed separate agreements with Sela rather than a joint contract. Joshua's deal explicitly stipulated that the bout must take place in the United Kingdom, whereas Fury's contained no such restriction. That distinction proved critical when organisers and broadcast partner Netflix began lobbying to move the show to the United States. Hearn acknowledged that virtually every other party involved preferred New York, with Matchroom even exploring what compensation would be required to waive the UK clause. For a moment, that stand-off threatened to scupper the entire event. Fury publicly accused Joshua of stalling and briefly floated the prospect of a trilogy fight with Oleksandr Usyk. But once Fury relented, organisers needed to find a British venue capable of satisfying the broadcast demands without leaving fans exposed to the British winter. Cardiff, almost by process of elimination, became the answer. Cardiff's Principality Stadium has a retractable roof The fight had initially been discussed for November but, with negotiations over the venue dragging on, it now looks set for December. Staging an open-air stadium fight in the UK at that time carries immense risk. While Wembley offers unmatched prestige, exposing tens of thousands of fans and a massive international broadcast operation to potentially freezing temperatures, wind and rain was deemed unacceptable. Moving the event indoors to an arena like London's O2 would eliminate weather risks, but at the cost of sacrificing tens of thousands of ticket sales. The Principality Stadium's retractable roof allows organisers to capture the immense scale, atmosphere and gate revenue of a stadium show while offering full protection from the elements. The venue's official seated capacity is just under 74,000, but boxing configurations allow for even larger crowds. Joshua has already proven he can sell out the venue, having defended his WBA and IBF titles there against Carlos Takam in front of nearly 80,000 fans in 2017 before adding the WBO belt against Joseph Parker five months later. We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor Fury says he is looking for new opponent, calls out Usyk 'Bring it on' - Cardiff businesses react to Fury vs Joshua rumours Perhaps the most difficult hurdle has been aligning the event with Netflix's preference to broadcast during prime-time hours in the United States. A projected UK ring walk of about 01:00 GMT - 20:00 on the US east coast - created a logistical headache for London. Wembley operates under a strict 23:00 event curfew. While Mayor of London Sadiq Khan offered his support and Wembley officials were open to discussions, securing the necessary approvals from Brent Council and local safety advisory groups for a 01:00 start presented an administrative hurdle. Cardiff offers a far smoother path. The Welsh Rugby Union, which owns and operates the Principality Stadium, previously indicated it would be delighted to host the fight and confirmed a late-night finish would not be a dealbreaker. While early-hours finishes still require extensive coordination around transport, policing and crowd management in the city centre, the venue already holds a clear precedent for late-night boxing. In 2007, Joe Calzaghe's super-middleweight unification victory over Mikkel Kessler did not start until 02:00 local time to satisfy American television network Showtime. For all the delays and frustrations that have plagued this rivalry over the past decade, Fury against Joshua remains the pinnacle of domestic boxing. Downgrading to an indoor arena would diminish the magnitude of the occasion. Crucially, taking the fight to America would have deprived domestic fans of a generational spectacle. British supporters have driven the commercial value of this rivalry for years, filling stadiums for both fighters' respective careers and following every collapsed negotiation. Staging the bout on home soil serves as a long-overdue reward for that loyalty, even if both men are now former world heavyweight champions. A stadium fight of this magnitude dominates the national conversation in a way a 04:00 New York or Las Vegas broadcast simply cannot, and local amateur boxing clubs could see a surge in interest when the country's biggest stars compete on home soil. Wales also has history of staging a huge fight between two British heavyweights: In 1993, Lennox Lewis defended his WBC title against Frank Bruno at Cardiff Arms Park - the venue that the Principality Stadium replaced. When the demands surrounding the event are broken down, Cardiff's emergence becomes easier to understand. Boxing schedule and results 2026 Watch every Born to Brawl episode Notific

title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists
description: The party says scrapping the scheme in 2021 left the UK less competitive than European destinations.
body: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch (left) and shadow culture secretary Rebecca Paul visited Bicester Village, a designer outlet shopping centre popular with tourists, to promote the policy The Conservative Party has pledged to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists from outside the European Union. The Tories said the decision to scrap the scheme in 2021 left the UK less competitive than European destinations. Leader Kemi Badenoch, who was a Treasury minister when the tax relief was abolished, said businesses were being "let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away". But Labour accused the party of "a spectacular U-turn". The VAT Retail Export Scheme - which allowed overseas visitors to get a VAT refund on items they had bought in Great Britain and took home in their luggage - was scrapped for non-EU visitors under the previous Conservative government in 2021, while it was also not extended for EU visitors. At the time, Badenoch said it was "a costly relief which does not benefit the whole of GB equally". However, the Conservatives have now set out plans to restore VAT refunds for eligible visitors from outside the EU. The party said that if evidence confirms the scheme "pays its way", this would be extended to visitors from the EU by the end of the next Parliament. It said the cost of reintroducing the scheme would be offset by cracking down on "NHS health tourism", including more consistent charging of patients ineligible for free treatment, minimum recovery targets for debts and requiring full repayment of debts before visa applications or renewals will be considered. The remaining costs would be funded from a package of savings set out by the Tories last year. Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping, businesses say Bring back duty-free perk to boost London - mayor The party also argued the move would benefit shops, hotels, restaurants and the wider tourism industry. It pointed to research by the Centre for Economics and Business Research (Cebr), which suggested fully restoring tax-free shopping for tourists could attract up to 2.35 million extra visitors and generate £4.1bn in extra spending. The report from earlier this month also estimated that for every £1 of VAT refunded, this could generate £1.54 in other taxes. Badenoch said: "We have iconic retailers, inventive designers and brilliant manufacturers, but they are being let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away. "Holidaymakers are choosing rival cities in other countries for the simple reason that it saves them money." Businesses have long called for tax-free shopping for tourists to be reintroduced, arguing they are at a disadvantage to other European countries. EU countries offer VAT refunds for non-EU visitors, while other European countries such as Switzerland have similar schemes. Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium, said: "Introducing a modern tax-free shopping scheme would help attract more international spending to the UK, supporting high streets, jobs and investment in towns and cities across the country. "Done properly, it would boost economic growth and deliver a net benefit to the Exchequer." However, a Labour spokesperson said: "Kemi Badenoch used to say tax-free shopping was a costly giveaway and now she's trying to sell it as an economic miracle. "If they really think it's such a great idea, they should explain why they scrapped it in the first place and how they'd pay for bringing it back." title: Three arrested in South Africa over one of nine women's body finds
description: The body of Jabulile Ntimba was the ninth to be found recently in an area east of Johannesburg.
body: Jabulile Ntimba's body was found by a road last Thursday Three suspects have been detained in South Africa in connection with the murder of a woman in an area east of Johannesburg – the last of nine recent cases in that region that has shone a spotlight on the level of violence against women in the country. Under pressure to solve the spate of murders which has involved victims' bodies being dumped on a roadside, police have described the arrests of the three – a man and two women - as a "breakthrough". Referring to all nine cases, acting police chief Lt Gen Puleng Dimpane said her officers were "working tirelessly to bring those responsible to justice". The three suspects are due in court on Monday morning. Their case relates to the death of Jabulile Ntimba, whose half-naked body was found wrapped in a sheet in Dawn Park last Thursday. Several of the recent victims were discovered partially clothed and with injuries, but police have stressed that they have not established whether all the deaths are connected or whether a serial killer is responsible. Addressing journalists on Monday, deputy police chief Lt Gen Tebello Mosikili said that "a team of analysts are working hard to see if there are links to all these cases" but the killing of Ntimba "appears to be an indication of a murder that stemmed from a relationship... this includes... a possible love triangle". South Africa has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world. It also has a very high murder rate and though officials statistics do not identify the gender of the victims, a recent estimate from the country's Human Rights Commission indicated that, on average, six women were murdered every day between April and June this year. The recent grim discoveries have sparked a national outcry about the scale of the problem and increased the feeling of insecurity for many women. title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?
description: Flights are affected again owing to air traffic control problems, so what are your rights if you're affected?
body: Flights in Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England have been affected by air traffic control issues – the second major disruption at UK airports in a few weeks. When a flight is cancelled or delayed, passengers affected have various rights, such as a refund or an alternative flight at no extra cost. However, these can vary depending on which carrier you are flying with and from where. Extra compensation is payable only when an airline is at fault, which is not the case with air traffic control problems. Here's what it means for you. Under UK law, airlines have a duty to look after you when flights are delayed or cancelled. The reason for the delay or cancellation does not matter. So anyone affected by the air transport delays will be eligible. That includes providing meals and accommodation, if necessary, and getting you to your destination. The airline should organise putting you on an alternative flight at no extra cost. Additional losses, such as unused accommodation, might require a claim to a credit card provider, if that was the payment option used. After that, a claim may need to go to your travel insurance provider, but there is no standard definition of what is covered. It may require a close look at the details of the policy to see what is covered and in which circumstances. Passengers are also being urged to heed travel advice from the UK government, external, as this can also affect travel insurance rights. UK law generally applies to your flight if you are flying from a UK airport on any airline, arriving at a UK airport on an EU or UK airline, or arriving at an airport in the EU on a UK airline. If your flight was coming into the UK on a non-UK or EU airline, then you should check the terms and conditions of your booking. If your flight is covered by UK law, your airline must let you choose between either getting a refund or being booked on to an alternative flight. That's regardless of how far in advance the cancellation was made. You can get your money back for any part of the ticket you have not used. So, if you booked a return flight and the outbound leg is cancelled, you can get the full cost of the return ticket refunded. If you still want to travel, your airline must find you an alternative flight. If another airline is flying to your destination significantly sooner, or there are other suitable modes of transport, then you have a right to be booked on to that alternative transport instead. How do I renew my UK passport and what is the 10-year rule?, external Three things you can do to stop EU border checks at the airport costing you If you are stuck abroad or at the airport because of a flight cancellation, airlines covered by UK legislation must also provide you with other assistance. a reasonable amount of food and drink (often in the form of vouchers) a way for you to communicate (often by refunding the cost of calls) free accommodation, if you have to stay overnight to fly the next day transport to and from the accommodation If your airline is unable to arrange assistance, you have the right to organise this yourself and claim back the cost later. The Civil Aviation Authority advises people to keep receipts and not spend more than necessary. Civil Aviation Authority: Delays and cancellations, external You are entitled to the same assistance as for a cancellation if your flight is delayed by more than two hours for a short-haul flight, three hours for a medium-haul, or four hours for a long-haul. If you are delayed by more than five hours and no longer want to travel, you can get a full refund. If you booked a package holiday with a company that is an ABTA member and your flight is cancelled, you are entitled to a suitable alternative flight or a full refund. ABTA: What are your rights?, external Disruption caused by "extraordinary circumstances" – which includes things like air traffic control issues, bad weather, strikes by airport staff, or conflict – does not entitle you to extra compensation. However, in other circumstances, when it is considered to be the airline's fault, you have a number of rights, external if your flight is covered under UK law. What you are entitled to depends on what caused the cancellation and how much notice you are given. If your flight is cancelled with less than two weeks' notice, you may be able to claim compensation based on the timings of the alternative flight you are offered. The amount you are entitled to also depends on how far you were travelling: for flights under 1,500km, such as Glasgow to Amsterdam, you can claim up to £220 per person for flights of 1,500km to 3,500km, such as East Midlands to Marrakesh, you can claim up to £350 per person for flights over 3,500km, such as London to New York, you can claim up to £520 per person Airlines will not refund you for loss of earnings. Travel insurance policies will not usually cover loss of earnings either. If you think you're going to be late back at work because of flight delays, you have a responsibility to let your employer know, legal experts say. You should agree with your employer how to deal with the absence – for example, by using annual leave or taking unpaid leave. Employers have no legal obligation to pay employees who are absent in this situation, experts say, unless it is stated in their contract. Have your travel plans been disrupted? Share your experience. title: Chris Martin joins busker for impromptu duet
description: Busker Hanny Junee says he did not realise who had joined him in Trafalgar Square until afterwards.
body: This video can not be played Chris Martin surprises Trafalgar Square busker with impromptu duet Coldplay singer Chris Martin joined a busker in central London for an impromptu duet. Hanny Junee was getting ready to sing Coldplay's hit Viva la Vida to a small audience in Trafalgar Square when the star joined him by the microphone and started singing along. But Junee said he did not realise who he was. He told the BBC: "I thought: 'This guy has amazing energy, nice vibe and a really good voice, he sounds really similar to Chris Martin.' "But I thought: 'Come on, Hanny, don't be ridiculous, of course it's not him, Chris Martin doesn't roam the streets of London.' Then he finished a verse and the next thing I know he's gone. It was magical." Junee added: "Afterwards some people came up to me and told me it really was Chris Martin. "It was amazing, it was like we connected purely through music, not fame." Speaking about Friday's duet, the full-time busker from South Korea said he had given his audience of about 20 a choice between Viva la Vida and a song by The Script. More hands went up for Viva la Vida, he said. A Coldplay fan himself, Junee said he could not believe what happened. He said he usually spent his days busking around Covent Garden, the London Eye and Trafalgar Square. Chris Martin, pictured in BBC Radio 2's Piano Room in 2024, has surprised his fans before It is not the first time Martin has surprised fans. In August 2025, he played an impromptu gig at a small pub in West Yorkshire, and in June 2022, he performed a song at a pub near Bath for a couple about to get married. title: Inside Djibouti refugee camp for thousands fleeing Houthi advance in Yemen
description: Fighting on Yemen's west coast has prompted thousands of people to flee by boat across the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
body: This video can not be played Fighting on Yemen's west coast has prompted thousands of people to flee by boat across the Bab al-Mandab Strait to Djibouti over the last ten days. The BBC's Frank Gardner visited a refugee camp in Obock, a small port town where officials are preparing for the arrival of up to 10,000 refugees. The UN International Organisation for Migration said people were ​travelling on overcrowded boats and arriving with very limited food and water. The crossings were sparked by an offensive by the Iran-backed Houthi movement to take control of a key island and seize the strategically important port of Mokha. title: Edwards signs short-term deal with Red Roses
description: Shaun Edwards has started a short-term coaching consultancy role with England women.
body: Edwards (left) has been approached by the Rugby Football Union in the past about a role with England's men's team, without ever being brought on board Shaun Edwards has started a short-term coaching consultancy role with England women. It is understood the 59-year-old will work with current Red Roses defence coach Sarah Hunter for the rest of their WXV Global Series matches, starting with New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. The news comes after England's 39-Test winning streak ended with a 26-26 draw against Canada last weekend. Englishman Edwards is one of the most decorated coaches in rugby union. He recently left his role as France men's defence coach, where he won three Six Nations titles. He has never previously worked for England's men or women. His playing career in rugby league saw him win 36 caps for Great Britain before coaching success with London Wasps and Wales and a six-year stint with France. This video can not be played Watch highlights: England 26-26 Canada On the appointment of Edwards, England head coach John Mitchell said: "Since his time with France ended, we have had a conversation about our game, and he expressed an interest in working in an international women's set-up for the first time. "He has a huge amount of respect for the Red Roses and what we stand for; he sees it as a privilege to join our environment. "His coaching credentials are exceptional and his experience at the highest level of the game speaks for itself. "Defensively, Sarah Hunter is relishing the opportunity to learn from him, alongside the rest of our coaching group, as we head into another exciting Test match against New Zealand." Last week, Edwards expressed his desire to return to coaching and be a part of next year's men's Six Nations. "I'm def­in­itely open to offers now, until I sort out a full-time role," he told the Daily Mail., external "I'm a proud Englishman and everybody loves to represent their country, don't they? I'm no different." title: Calvin Harris recognised for 1.6m world record DJ set crowd
description: An estimated 1.6m people attended the Dumfries DJ's set in Sao Paulo in Brazil earlier this year.
body: Harris has been recognised by Guinness World Records on a number of occasions Scottish DJ Calvin Harris has been celebrating writing his name into the record books after performing for an estimated 1.6m people in Sao Paulo earlier this year. The musician from Dumfries received recognition from Guinness World Records (GWR) for the largest attendance for a DJ set by a single artist. He took to social media to highlight the award for what he described as a "truly insane day" which he said could only have happened in Brazil. GWR said it had been reported that his headline appearance had forced the closure of the Rua da Consolação with some fans fainting in the heat. This article contains content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. You may want to read Meta’s Instagram cookie policy, external and privacy policy, external before accepting. To view this content choose ‘accept and continue’. Harris has already been recognised for a number of other records in the past. In 2014, GWR presented him with a certificate for most top 10 hits on the UK singles chart from one album for 18 Months which produced no fewer than nine. It also lists him as the highest paid DJ in one year for his earnings between June 2015 and 2016. GWR said Harris had turned Sao Paulo into "one massive street party" by climbing on board a carnival float for his performance on 8 February 2026. Wearing a Brazilian football shirt with the name Calvinho on the back he worked his way through a setlist featuring many of his biggest hits. The record book also noted that a similar-sized crowd attended Madonna's free concert on Copacabana Beach in May 2024 during her Celebration Tour. title: World Gurning Championship winners crowned
description: The World Gurning Championship is held annually in the small Cumbrian town of Egremont.
body: Will Mellor came second in the men's competition Actor Will Mellor has come a surprise second in the World Gurning Championships, pipped to the main prize by local man Ged Eccles who had come close but never before won. Part of the annual Egremont Crab Fair in Cumbria, which began in 1267, the gurning competition has been a fixture since the 1500s. Competitors are judged on their ability to pull the ugliest or most grotesque face. The Hollyoaks and Mr Bates vs The Post Office star won second place in the men's competition after attending as part of a programme he was filming. Eccles said he felt "ecstatic" to have finally won the men's competition. It was his first victory since becoming the junior champion in 1985. He came second in 2023 and was third in 2016 and 2009 and said he believed he had won this year because of the extra practice he had put in. Ged Eccles won this year's world championships "I practise in front of a mirror for maybe three to four hours a day," he said. "I've been doing that since the end of May." He said he did this to loosen up his neck, cheekbone and jaw bone muscles in order to get his lip on to his nose. "And that's what I did," he said. Eccles said he hoped to defend his title next year and that he planned to continue gurning "until the day I can't do it anymore". One of the event's organisers, Dan Nixon, said it was good to see Eccles finally win. He said there were about 50 entrants to the men's, women's and junior versions of the competition and that up to 800 people had attended. "I think everyone in Egremont takes part in the Crab Fair in some way," he said. Claire Lister is a seasoned winner, Dan Nixon said Local woman Claire Lister won the women's competition again after losing her crown last year. The nine-time champion said: "I'm absolutely delighted to have won again, I'm really proud and it still feels just as special every time. "It's just a bit of fun and keeps the Egremont Crab Fair tradition going." Lister said she does not train or practise for the competition but just turns up on the day and gives it her best. "I think after doing it for so many years it just comes naturally to me now," she said. Nixon described her as "a seasoned winner". The competition's organising committee have already started planning next year's event which will be its 760th. "We're very much hoping that it's going to be a really, really big spectacular," he said. title: D-Day veteran who survived capture dies aged 101
description: Kenneth Hay was an "extraordinary gentleman whose remarkable life will never be forgotten", the British Normandy Memorial says.
body: Normandy veteran Kenneth Hay was an "extraordinary gentleman", the British Normandy Memorial said Normandy veteran Kenneth Hay, who survived being captured just weeks after D-Day and spent years educating children about World War Two, has died aged 101. Hay, from Upminster in east London, served in the 4th Dorset Infantry Regiment. He was captured a month after the allied invasion of northern France and survived a 1,000-mile (1,609km) forced march in eastern Europe until he was liberated by US forces. His death was announced on Sunday by the British Normandy Memorial, for which he was an ambassador. The organisation said he was an "extraordinary gentleman whose remarkable life will never be forgotten". In its statement on social media, the British Normandy Memorial added: "His passion for education was unwavering. "The countless schoolchildren whose lives he touched with his stories of courage and resilience nicknamed him 'Grandad Ken'. "We extend our most sincere condolences to Ken's sons Chris and Jeremy, all the Hay family and his very many friends." Hay, pictured in 2025 at the British Normandy Memorial in Ver-sur-Mer, France, served in the 4th Dorset Infantry Regiment D-Day, on 6 June 1944, saw British, American and Canadian troops storm beaches along the Normandy coastline to begin the liberation of France from Nazi occupation. Hay had landed at Courseulles-sur-Mer just days after and was captured by the German 12th SS Panzer Division during a night patrol on 7-8 July. He was taken to Zabrze in Poland, where he was put to work as a prisoner of war in a coal mine. Speaking of the capture in 2024, Hay recalled his first feelings were of "dread" and "fear". "We went out on night patrol, was supposed to be doing a blow up of a self-propelled gun in no man's land, but in fact, it was behind their lines," he said. "So they let us through and then very unfriendly, they sealed it and wouldn't let us back, so we had a battle. "We had 30 [that] went out on our patrol, 16 including my brother, who was a corporal, got back, five of us got captured and then presumably nine got killed." As the Russians approached, the prisoners were marched to a new location, approximately 1,000 miles away, during which many of them died. During the three-month march, Hay said he once "lay down to die" after it became too painful to continue, but two friends turned back for him and lifted him with an "arm around each shoulder". This video can not be played 'Most people see names, I see faces' says Normandy veteran Kenneth Hay Eventually they were liberated by American troops and Hay returned to the UK, via Reims, on 4 May 1945. Recalling the moment he made it to his mother's house in Barking, he said: "They came running down the road to greet me." After the war, he was appointed an MBE for services to the community and received the Legion d'Honneur, France's highest order of merit. Hay regularly visited British schools to share stories of the war and answer questions, saying he believed it was his "duty to pass it on". title: Flights in UK delayed by 'technical issue' with air traffic control in Scotland
description: Engineers are investigating the issue at the Prestwick Centre which handles air traffic control across Scotland and the north of England.
body: Edinburgh is one of the airports affected by the incident A "technical issue" with air traffic control in Scotland is causing delays to flights in the UK. The national air traffic service (Nats) said engineers had been called in to deal with the issue at the Prestwick Centre in South Ayrshire which handles air traffic control across Scotland and the north of England. The service said the issue was not related to a software defect that led to the cancellation of 2,000 flights across the UK earlier this month. Passengers have taken to social media to confirm they are experiencing delays at Glasgow, Prestwick and Edinburgh airports. Dundee and Benbecula airports have also confirmed flights are impacted. A spokesperson for Edinburgh Airport said: "We are experiencing some delays due to the Nats issue at Prestwick Centre. "We are monitoring the situation closely and are working with Nats as they work to resolve the issue." A spokesperson for Ryanair said they had been notified of a Nats "equipment failure" affecting airspace above Scotland and northern England. They said it was impacting flights to and from the UK and Ireland. A Nats spokesperson said: "Our engineers are continuing to investigate the issue at our Prestwick centre in Scotland. "Airports south of Manchester are broadly unaffected, however flights heading north and flights departing Scottish airports are currently subject to some delay." The spokesperson apologised for the disruption and urged passengers to check with their airline for more information. Lewis Fraser from Inverness is onboard a flight stuck on the runway at Glasgow Airport. He told BBC News: "We boarded the flight as normal but were immediately told we were delayed. "The latest update was around half an hour ago to say we might be waiting another hour and 45 minutes. Some passengers have left the plane in the last few minutes." He is travelling to Heathrow to get a connecting flight to Chicago but said making his connection seemed "unlikely". Have you been affected by the disruption to flights? title: Gavin and Stacey co-stars support Strictly debut, says Melanie Walters
description: Walters, best known for playing Gwen West in the BBC comedy, is partnered with professional Aljaz Skorjanec.
body: Melanie Walters and Aljaz Skorjanec performed together for the first time on Saturday's show Actor Melanie Walters has said her Gavin and Stacey co-stars have been "hugely supportive" of her Strictly Come Dancing debut, with Joanna Page "very excited" for her to take to the ballroom floor. The screen and stage star, 64, best known for playing Gwen West in the BBC comedy, is partnered with professional Aljaz Skorjanec, 36, in the new series of the dance programme. Walters said being paired with Skorjanec was a "dream come true" after the pair performed together for the first time at Saturday's launch show. She said her Gavin and Stacey co-stars had sent her "lovely messages, especially from Jo [Page], who's just very excited". When asked if she would be bringing any of her character from the comedy onto the ballroom floor, she added: "I've got no idea, this is Aljaz's department. "I've got no idea what's going to happen on that ballroom." Walters told the Press Association it was "mind-boggling" to be asked to join the series and that it was "a bit out of my comfort zone". "I've not been one for doing panel shows or quiz shows or anything," she said. Melanie Walters said her Gavin and Stacey co-stars had been very supportive "So, it's now me, Melanie Walters, which is not what I'm used to putting out there, because I'm quite a private person. I just thought, 'no, let's tick that box'. "And basically, I really want to learn to dance properly. Always have. "Getting weekly masterclasses. You couldn't ask for anything better." Walters starred in Gavin and Stacey from its launch in 2007 and reprised her role for a 2024 Christmas special. Her television work also includes roles in Coronation Street, Beyond Paradise, Being Human, Hollyoaks, Biff And Chip, and Doc Martin, while her film credits include Submarine, Resistance, High Tide and Save The Cinema. On stage, she has appeared in productions such as The Importance Of Being Earnest, Blood Brothers, Twelfth Night, Educating Rita and What's New Pussycat?. She also recently appeared in two series of the BBC's crime mystery series Death Valley. title: Lib Dems demand action over increase in child birth injuries
description: Sir Ed Davey pledged to spend £600m a year on maternity services if the Lib Dems were in government.
body: Health spokesperson Helen Morgan met parents and babies to discuss maternity care The government must not ignore a "national safety scandal" in maternity services, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey has said, as figures suggest life-altering childbirth injuries in England have reached record levels. Lib Dem analysis of NHS figures showed the number of women suffering potentially life-threatening levels of blood loss is the highest ever recorded in England. Three in every 100 women suffered serious tearing injuries requiring emergency surgery in the first half of this year, something Sir Ed said was a "devastating indictment of our NHS maternity services". The government is expected to publish a new national maternity and neonatal action plan by the end of the year. Speaking to BBC Breakfast at the Lib Dem annual conference in Brighton, Davey pledged to spend £600m a year on maternity services if in government. He said £1.3bn a year was currently being spent on "failure" through negligence compensation payouts for poor maternity services, but said this investment should go towards prevention instead. Calling for more senior midwives and consultants, he said: "Our current maternity staff are run ragged - they're massively overstretched. "That's the best way, all the evidence shows, to make sure maternity units are safe," he added. "It is a scandal at the moment - we've seen inquiry after inquiry. So many women are suffering injuries at birth and we're seeing the loss of babies too; it is a tragedy as well as a scandal." He said ministers "cannot turn a blind eye to this national safety scandal" and mothers "deserve safe, compassionate care". The party pointed to Care Quality Commission (CQC) survey data showing one-in-10 women, about 54,000, were left alone during late stages of labour or childbirth last year, which the Lib Dems said was due to lack of training and staff shortages. More than 8,000 women had postpartum haemorrhages with blood loss of more than 1.5l since the start of this year, more than double the number over the equivalent period in 2021, the party's analysis of NHS figures suggests. Rates of major haemorrhage peaked between April and June this year, while 32.7 women per thousand needed emergency treatment. The rate of third or fourth degree vaginal tears during childbirth has risen by 29% in the last five years, according to the analysis. The Lib Dem health spokesperson Helen Morgan, who successfully campaigned for an independent maternity commissioner to drive improvements, said reports on previous maternity scandals were "gathering dust". "Years after the Shrewsbury and Telford scandal which devastated my community - my neighbours and friends - women continue to suffer," she said. "This must be the moment we say 'enough'." A review in 2022 found catastrophic failures at Shrewsbury and Telford NHS Trust (SaTH) over 20 years may have led to the deaths of more than 200 babies. The trust apologised and said it had already put in measures to prevent a repeat. A Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) spokesperson said the review to be published later this year will bring together the recommendations from the Baroness Amos, Donna Ockenden, and Lady Justice Thirlwall inquiries, set clear priorities and hold the system to account for delivering improved outcomes. "Every woman deserves safe maternity care and the new health secretary has made this issue a personal priority," they said. "Through the National Maternity and Neonatal Taskforce that she is chairing, this government will deliver the reforms needed to ensure the very highest standards of safety and care for every mother and baby." England's first statutory Maternity and Neonatal Commissioner will be appointed to ensure the voices of women, babies and families are at the heart of national policy making. The DHSC is also extending Martha's Rule to every maternity and neonatal ward to ensure that any reports of deterioration from patients or their families are acted upon, and has invested £187m since April 2025 to address critical safety risks in the maternity and neonatal estate. A Labour Party spokesperson said: "Ed Davey was part of the coalition government that tore up the national standards for maternity services that Yvette Cooper is now having to restore. "He never raised any objections to that decision at the time, and he has never apologised since. Until he does so, his words on this issue will ring hollow." Baby scandal: The mothers who died Ed Davey calls for immediate 10p cut to fuel duty Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth Addressing the criticism of Julian Brazil, Leader of Devon County Council, the party who said on Sunday he thought the party was "sleepwalking into irrelevance" , Sir Ed told BBC Breakfast there was always going to be criticism of leadership as the party gets bigger. "We have grown really fast under my leadership , with record number of MPs and running more councils," he said. "When you have a bigger party you can't please everyone all the time." title: Public confidence 'damaged' by on-the-run killer case, says Long
description: Gary Anderson remains at large a week after he absconded while attending his father's funeral in Derry.
body: Naomi Long says is to speak in the Assembly on Monday about the circumstances surrounding on-the-run killer Gary Anderson's compassionate temporary release from Maghaberry Prison Public confidence in the justice system has been "damaged" by the circumstances surrounding the temporary release from prison of convicted murderer Gary Anderson, Justice Minister Naomi Long has said. Anderson, who is one of two brothers jailed for life in 2023 for the 2018 murder of Karol Kelly in Londonderry, remains at large a week after he absconded while attending his father's funeral in Derry last Monday. Naomi Long, who is to meet the murder victim's family, is ordering an independent review into the circumstances surrounding Anderson's release from Maghaberry Prison. That happened after a court overturned a decision by the prison service to refuse him permission to attend the funeral. A day before the funeral last Monday, a judge granted Anderson a two-hour compassionate temporary release (CTR) from Maghaberry Prison to attend it. The funeral service took place at St Mary's Church in the Creggan area of Derry last Monday morning. Anderson was not given permission to attend cremation in Letterkenny, County Donegal, in the Republic of Ireland that afternoon. At some stage on Monday morning, he absconded from his court-approved civilian chaperone. Gary Anderson, who is serving a 15-year sentence for the murder of Karol Kelly, remains on the run CTR can be granted to prisoners when a family member has died or is seriously ill, but the decision to release them takes into account the circumstances of the case and any risks involved. Questions have been raised over the granting of Anderson's CTR following the publication of the full 15-page judgement from the judicial review into the Prison Service's decision., external The judgement found that the decision to refuse Anderson's request was based on inaccurate information about the risk he posed. The decision had been taken by the duty governor at Maghaberry Prison. In his judgement, Mr Justice Rooney found that an internal assessment of Anderson's likelihood of reoffending had been recorded at a higher level than the score held on the Prison Service's internal system. A legal representative for the Prison Service told the court that the increased score had come from a colleague rather than the duty governor's personal knowledge. When the system was checked, Anderson's score was 27, indicating a medium likelihood of reoffending, rather than 32, which had been recorded as a high likelihood in the decision letter. The judge found that the duty governor "clearly took account of this incorrect information" when assessing the risks and considering whether the decision was proportionate. He invited the duty governor to reconsider the decision, but that offer was declined. The judge described the decision not to review it as "somewhat surprising" and he granted Anderson temporary release subject to a number of conditions, finding that the Prison Service's decision was "flawed" and had taken into account "irrelevant and incorrect factors". The judge said the failure to secure and take account of the correct risk assessment was unlawful. Speaking to BBC Radio Foyle's North West Today programme on Monday, Long said a procedural failing by the Departmental Solicitor's Office (DSO), meant prison officials were not told that a judge had offered them the chance to reconsider their decision not to release Anderson. Long said that the DSO had acknowledged a "procedural failing on their part" and this was "not communicated at any stage". "We have identified that that offer was not passed on to the decision-makers within Prison Service at that time and so we have only become aware of it when the full judgement was actually published and we were then able to refer to the transcripts. "I'm setting up a completely independent review because our understanding would be that it would be for our legal advisors from the department, the Departmental Solicitor's Office (DSO) to come back to us and there was contact between Northern Ireland Prison Service and our solicitor during this period but it didn't include any reflection that the judge was offering an opportunity to reconsider or re-evaluate or provide additional information and that's absolutely key. "It's a normal process when it goes to court that the judge may ask for more information, may ask for more clarity and that offer was not made to Prison Service and therefore we were in a situation where it rested in the hands of the judge and the judge in good faith made the decision based on the information that he had." Speaking on Monday, Long apologised to the family of Karol Kelly and acknowledged the impact Gary Anderson's release and subsequent absconding from prison has had. She said she was "desperately sorry that they have been put through this trauma as a result of whatever has happened" and said she was commissioning and independent review. "Whatever miscommunication, whatever poor information, they should not have been subjected to this ongoing trauma and distress, and I can only apologise genuinely for that. "I will be meeting them, obviously subject to their wishes. I received a letter last week from Mark H Durkan, and I wrote back and said that I would be happy to meet with the family at their earliest convenience, and hopefully that will be able to happen soon. "I don't want them to be drawn into this, I don't want them to feel any further distress." Long has said all relevant facts must be established and carefully considered and is to update MLAs on Monday about the case. "I am concerned enough about this case and I think it's important to say by the impact that it has had on the Kelly family and they are first and foremost in mind at the moment," she said. title: Palmer set to withdraw from England squad after recall
description: Chelsea forward Cole Palmer is set to withdraw from England's squad for the upcoming Nations League matches because of a minor injury.
body: Cole Palmer has two goals and two assists in the Premier League this season Chelsea forward Cole Palmer is set to withdraw from England's squad for the upcoming Nations League matches because of a minor injury. The 24-year-old had been recalled by manager Thomas Tuchel having been controversially left out of the Three Lions' squad for the World Cup. Tuchel previously said Palmer had a "point to prove" and needed "to step up" to "keep his shirt and justify the nomination". However, the Blues forward will now miss the extended international break in which England play four games. The Three Lions face World Cup winners Spain at Wembley on Saturday, 26 September, then travel to the Czech Republic (29 September) and Croatia (3 October) before hosting the Czechs on 6 October. Palmer's withdrawal comes after he played the full game for Chelsea in their 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Friday. Following a summer off after missing out on World Cup selection, he has started six of Chelsea's seven games and played the full 90 minutes in five of them - scoring four goals and providing two assists. Palmer was hampered by a recurring groin injury in 2025-26, which former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca - who is now boss at Manchester City - said did not make sense. Palmer last played for England in their 1-0 friendly defeat by Japan in March. title: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
description: The groups have been active in Ethiopia's most populous regions for years and now say they will work together.
body: There have been renewed tensions in the northern Tigray region Several of the rebel groups which have been fighting the Ethiopian authorities in different parts of the country have announced they have formed an alliance to remove the government in Addis Ababa. The alliance brings together the Fano militia in Amhara, the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and four other smaller groupings in a coalition named Alliance for Survival. The seven groups accuse Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government of presiding over "war, genocide, mass destruction, and utter poverty", claiming Ethiopia is at risk of disintegration. Federal authorities have not yet responded. Ethiopia has faced years of armed conflict in Oromia and Amhara, the most populous states in the country. There have also been renewed tensions in the northern Tigray region, where a two-year civil war left hundreds of thousands dead and displaced millions. An African-Union peace deal ended that war in 2022, but there have been fears of a return to a full-scale conflict, with both sides accusing each other of violating that agreement. Besides Oromia, Amhara and Tigray, the new alliance also includes groups based in three other regions - Ogaden, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz – making up a half of Ethiopia's 12 regional states. Amhara's Fano group fought alongside federal forces during the Tigray war. It however turned against the federal government in an armed insurgency less than a year after the war ended, after refusing government orders to disarm. The government has been fighting the OLA since 2018. The announcement of the Alliance for Survival coalition comes months after reports of an alleged alliance between TPLF and neighbouring Eritrea. Abiy responded by saying he had faith in Ethiopia's "defensive capabilities". "Even if others were added, we do not have an iota of fear regarding Ethiopia's sovereignty," he told lawmakers in July. The country held a general election in June, with Abiy's Prosperity Party retaining its overwhelming parliamentary majority, despite the poll being overshadowed by conflict, accusations of repression and little participation by opposition parties. The Fano and OLA rebel groups rejected the election and its results. The Tigray region and its six million inhabitants were completely excluded from the poll. title: Sydney policeman allegedly disguised himself as Uber Eats rider before murders
description: Beaumont Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to the 2024 murder of his ex-partner and his new boyfriend.
body: Luke Davies (left) and Jesse Baird were allegedly murdered by Beaumont Lamarre-Condon in Feburary 2024 A former police officer accused of using his work gun to kill a Sydney couple was driven by a "jealous infatuation" with his ex, a court has heard. Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to two charges of domestic violence-related murder and one of aggravated break and enter. Prosecutors allege Lamarre-Condon shot his ex-partner, 26-year-old TV presenter Jesse Baird, and Baird's new partner Luke Davies, a 29-year-old Qantas flight attendant, at a home in the Sydney suburb of Paddington in 2024. The couple's bodies were found in a rural area 200km away, hidden in surfboard bags. The trial is expected to run for three months. In his opening address on Monday, prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC described how Lamarre-Condon had developed an "obsessive and jealous infatuation" with Baird after a brief romantic relationship. It manifested itself in a "range of compulsive behaviour", Hatfield said, which escalated when Baird ended all contact in November 2023. The barrister said Lamarre-Condon used a friend's phone to message Baird and claim he had cancer, stalked his ex-lover, and tampered with his car in the weeks after their break-up. Beaumont Lamarre-Condon is accused of murdering his former partner, Jesse Baird, and Baird's new boyfriend Luke Davies On the day of the alleged murders, Lamarre-Condon had set his alarm for 04.30 local time, Hatfield claimed, and sent a text to a friend which read: "I'll try to call you tonight and update you... there's no sign I'm doing it". Lamarre-Condon then switched to a burner phone, picked up a rental car and waited outside Baird's home for three hours dressed as an Uber driver, the prosecution alleged. He had previously bought a surfboard bag to dispose of Baird's body, Hatfield said. After entering Baird's home with a key he had previously obtained, Lamarre-Condon shot Baird in the kitchen and then killed Davies in the bedroom as he was trying to call emergency services for help, the court was told. Hatfield said that the accused had planned Baird's murder, and killed Davies so as to "eliminate him as a witness". In the hours and days after the alleged killings, Lamarre-Condon tried to cover up the murder, Hatfield said, including sending messages from Baird's mobile phone. The aggravated break and enter charge that Lamarre-Condon is facing refers to an incident in August 2023 where it's alleged he broke into Baird's home and stole his phone and wallet. Hatfield also told the court that Lamarre-Condon had earlier offered to plead guilty to a single charge of manslaughter relating to Baird's death but this was rejected. Police were first alerted to the alleged murders after bloodied items belonging to Baird and Davies were found in a bin in Sydney's south. Later that week, Lamarre-Condon handed himself in to a police station and was charged. Eight days after the alleged killings took place, authorities found the couple's bodies. Lamarre-Condon was sacked by New South Wales Police in the weeks after he was charged with the alleged murders. Before the opening address on Monday, a 15-member jury was selected, with the judge, Justice Natalie Adams, explaining that three extra people were chosen - a jury is typically made up of 12 people - as a contingency for sickness and other unforeseen circumstances. title: Temperatures forecast to hit 25C but heatwave chances fall
description: While temperatures are expected to rise this week, it won't be warm enough to be classed as an official heatwave.
body: It is set to turn warmer across the United Kingdom over the next few days, with temperatures peaking around 25C (77F). Widely, however, temperatures will climb into the low 20s Celsius, which is around five degrees higher than the average for late September. It will also stay mostly dry with some sunny spells, though rain is likely at times across northern and western parts of the UK. The warmth is likely to last for much of the week across England and Wales while it gets a bit cooler in Scotland and Northern Ireland. High pressure is building across the UK and this means the weather will become more settled with brighter conditions. After a chilly start on Monday morning, with sunshine and light winds across much of England and Wales, temperatures will climb into the low 20s. Even with more cloud in Scotland and Northern Ireland, it will turn warmer with highs also reaching 18 to 22C. It will also start to feel more humid again. That more humid air combined with light winds across England and Wales into Tuesday means it will start off rather misty and foggy with areas of low cloud for some. Once the sun has broken through though, it will feel warmer still. Temperatures could peak at around 24 or 25C in south-east England, but reach the low 20s Celsius in many other parts of England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Eastern Scotland. The highest temperature though will be determined by how much the cloud breaks allowing the strong September sunshine through. 2026 has already been a record-breaking year for the number of days above 25C, with last week exceeding the record of 89 days set in 1959. Temperatures will rise across the UK on Tuesday and while turning less warm on Wednesday, the warmth will remain especially in south-east England. At the start of the week, high pressure will largely block rain-bearing weather systems from crossing the UK. However, some rain is possible on Tuesday as a weather front moves into western Scotland and the west of Northern Ireland. This will become more substantial by Wednesday, stretching across Scotland, Northern Ireland, Wales and western areas of England, as high pressure is nudged a bit further east. It will also turn a bit cooler here with temperatures back to around the average of 14 to 18C. Drier and warmer conditions will likely persist in east and south-east England with temperatures once again reaching the mid-20s Celsius. While temperatures may go down by a few degrees for the end of the week, it will still be warmer than average with temperatures in the high teens to low 20s. The settled, drier weather will also likely last in southern and eastern England too with little rain for places continuing to experience drought conditions. The warmer spell of weather this week will not meet the criteria to become a heatwave. The Met Office defines this as temperatures reaching 26 to 28C - dependent on location - for three consecutive days. With temperatures expected to be more like 20-25C, it will fall short of the threshold. However, these temperatures are notably warm for late September and it could therefore feel like summer has made a return. Warm spells at the end of September are fairly usual as the UK can still get hot air transported from southern Europe or North Africa with any southerly airflow. The last week of September also looks like it will be slightly warmer than average overall across the UK, despite being less warm than this week. The forecast further ahead and into October is more uncertain but signs are it could start to feel more like autumn with wetter and windier weather becoming more dominant. title: 'No surprises' as results emerge in Russian parliamentary election
description: Preliminary results suggest that Kremlin-backed United Russia is on course to retain its constitutional majority.
body: This video can not be played Preliminary results from Russia's elections suggest that the party backed by President Vladimir Putin, United Russia, will maintain its grip on parliament. The outcome comes as no surprise, according to the BBC's Russia editor, Steve Rosenberg, who has been following the elections from Moscow. The vote comes after more than four and a half years of war against Ukraine, a conflict which has seen huge battlefield losses for the Russian army and sparked economic hardship. The only anti-war party, Yabloko, was removed the ballot in the run-up to polling day – although some candidates remained in some constituencies. title: 'Far from their best' to 'a joy to watch' - ranking Premier League teams' start to season
description: Five matches into the league season, which teams in the Premier League have impressed so far and who have disappointed?
body: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland (left) and Manchester United defender Harry Maguire There is now a three-week international break with no Premier League games until 10 October. We are five matches into the league season and there is a long way to go in the campaign, but which teams have impressed so far and who have disappointed? You can have your say in the comments at the bottom of the page. Arsenal: Solid start to their title defence until they were ripped apart by Brighton having survived a penalty scare at Sunderland. 7 Aston Villa: Signs they are beginning to move in the right direction after losing so many key players during the transfer window. 6 Bournemouth: If games lasted 80 minutes the Cherries would be near the top of the table. Need to cut out conceding so late. 6 Brentford: Demolished Spurs and Chelsea without fuss during a highly impressive unbeaten start. Can they keep it up and challenge for Europe? 8 Brighton: Kings of entertainment after hitting 16 goals in five top-flight games, including three against champions Arsenal. A joy to watch. 9 Chelsea: After a strong start under Xabi Alonso, the Blues have lost two of their past three - and were picked apart by Brentford. Are they really moving in the right direction? 6 Coventry City: You could hear the sighs of relief in the away end at Nottingham Forest on Saturday. Will Frank Lampard's side kick on after that win? 6 Crystal Palace: Room for improvement after one win and three defeats. 5 Everton: Despite a transfer window to forget, David Moyes has made the Toffees hard to beat. 6 Fulham: Decent draws against Liverpool and Manchester United but need a win. Ipswich (away) followed by Hull (home), Coventry (away) and Crystal Palace (home) offer hope when they return from the international break. 5 Hull City: To have eight points from a tough opening five fixtures is an excellent return, including beating Manchester United and drawing with Aston Villa and Chelsea. 8 Ipswich Town: Defensively vulnerable but two late winners, against Sunderland and Crystal Palace, have earned them six points and shown their fighting spirit. 5 Leeds United: Fifth in the league, unbeaten and with the joint-best defensive record. They showed what they are capable of with a superb 4-1 win over Newcastle. 7 Liverpool: Unbeaten but have been far from their best. Three clean sheets in their past three games, but more is expected from Andoni Iraola's side. 6 Manchester City: Five league games, five victories. Managed to win at Manchester United despite going down to 10 men midway through the first half. With Erling Haaland already top scorer, City fans will expect a real push to win the league. 9 Manchester United: Disappointing performances to lose at Hull and draw at a Fulham side who were bottom of the league. Their only win so far came against Ipswich and they were denied a victory at Everton by a late equaliser. 4 Newcastle United: A mixed bag under new manager Matthias Jaissle. They impressed in a draw against Liverpool, won comfortably at Tottenham, but were also terrible in a loss at Leeds, although they responded well to beat Hull. 6 Nottingham Forest: Their best results have come away, drawing at Liverpool and winning at Aston Villa. But their home form will be a huge worry - yet to score a goal and with only one point from three matches at the City Ground. 5 Sunderland: After coming seventh in 2025-26, Sunderland fans will have wanted a better start to this season. The Black Cats gave good accounts of themselves against Arsenal and Manchester City, but lost both matches. 5 Tottenham Hotspur: After spending more than £300m in the summer, Spurs have been poor, failing to score in their opening four league matches. Supporters will be demanding an instant improvement after the international break. 2 Palmer set to withdraw from England squad after recall Premier League review: Who's had the best start & who has the most work to do?
